messages:
alex: Quick follow-up from the allocator ownership RFC — I prototyped a light handoff API where the runtime can 'relinquish' residency for a region and the offloader can 'claim' it with a lease. Thoughts?

mira: interesting. what's the lease semantics? do we want fast reclaim vs long-term demotion? :thinking:

alex: idea is short leases (100-500ms) for streaming workloads, longer leases (seconds) for pinned embeddings. runtime offers `lease_hint(duration_ms, flags)` and offloader returns `claim_result {accepted|deferred|rejected}`.

sam: careful about thrash. if leases are too short we end up ping-ponging pages. need hysteresis.

lee: +1 to hysteresis. maybe keep an LRU score bump on reclaim so runtime won't immediately re-request. also think about NUMA locality when offloading to host memory vs remote node.

alex: exactly — planned: lease includes `locality_penalty` and `reclaim_cooldown_ms`. offloader sets cooldown when it sees high churn. pseudo:```
// runtime -> offloader
lease_hint({addr, size, desired_ms:200, flags:HOT|PERSISTENT})
// offloader -> runtime
claim_result(accepted, cooldown_ms=1200)
```

mira: can we surface cooldown in telemetry? we need per-tenant churn and reclaim counters for cost accounting.

sam: perf question — how does this interact with our KV cache and prefix reuse? if we offload a prefix that is later reused, recompute cost may be worse than keeping it. need cheap estimator.

lee: we already have hit-rate histograms on prefixes. offloader can consult a short-term reuse predictor (exponential EWMA) before accepting claims. cheaper than full eval.

alex: good plan. propose the acceptance logic: if predicted_reuse_prob > threshold -> reject; else accept and set cooldown proportional to predicted_reuse_prob. thresholds per-tenant.

mira: edge-case: prefetchers. If runtime prefetches pages for upcoming tokens, offloader must avoid accepting those. we need a flag `no_offload` on leases.

alex: added flag in API. `lease_hint(..., flags: NO_OFFLOAD)`

sam: implementation nit — keep API C-friendly: `int lease_hint(void* addr, size_t len, uint32_t flags, uint32_t desired_ms)` returning token id. `claim_result(token, status, cooldown_ms)` callback.

lee: also include `reason_code` in claim_result so we know if rejection due to capacity, hotness, or policy (tenant). helps ops.

alex: agreed. ops-wise we should auto-escalate to a fallback model when acceptance rate drops below some SLA. offload-bot can emit alerts.

offload-bot: alert: offload-acceptance-rate < 0.6 for tenant=acme-corp in us-west-2 (last 5m).

mira: perfect — link that into Console so product teams can see cost/latency tradeoff.

sam: concern: memory accounting. when offloader accepts claim, who owns the memory for billing? runtime or offloader? we should transfer ownership atomically in accounting.

alex: transfer-on-claim. runtime decrements resident_tokens, offloader increments. will add metrics: `claims_transferred`, `claim_reverts` (when runtime reclaims early).

lee: test plan: 1) microbench with synthetic churn, 2) end-to-end with chat workload, 3) tenant fairness sim. Also add a chaos test where offloader randomly defers claims.

alex: timeline: I'll land API proto next week, sam can wire metrics, mira will add Console surfaces, lee will run perf sims. Assign follow-ups?

mira: I'll own Console dashboards.

sam: I'll hook metrics and add EWMA reuse predictor.

lee: I'll write the perf harness and run before the next sprint review.

alex: thanks. one more question: are we ok with the binary accepted/deferred/rejected tri-state, or add a `partial_accept(size)` variant for large regions?

sam: partial_accept seems useful for big tensors. offloader may only accept a subset. keep the token semantics: token maps to ranges.

mira: keep the UI simple — Console should show accepted size vs requested size.

lee: small ops doc item: document `claim_result.reason_code` values and cooldown heuristics.

alex: will draft RFC addendum with API signatures and a small example flow. will ping everyone for review. :thumbsup:

mira: :thumbsup:

sam: thanks — excited to try this out.

lee: cool, closing loop.

offload-bot: deploy: allocator-handoff-probe/1 -> staging succeeded (build 7893)
